transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you’d like to talk about or get help with?

Hi, doctor. Well, I’m here because things at work have really been getting to me lately. We got a new operations manager, and ever since they started, they've been picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. 

It's gotten to the point where I just can’t seem to leave work at work anymore. I come home all wound up, I end up snapping at my husband, and I just lie awake at night replaying our meetings in my head. And then the next day, I find myself second-guessing these routine quality calls that I used to make without any trouble at all. It's just really wearing me down.
Outside of work, do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about other areas of your life, like your relationships, health, or other responsibilities?

No, not really. Um, my health is fine, and everything else is pretty stable. I mean, I feel terrible that I've been short with my husband lately, but I'm not worried about our marriage or anything like that. We're solid. 

It really is just the job. If it weren't for this situation at the plant, I think everything else in my life would be completely fine. It's just that the stress from work is sort of... bleeding over into everything else.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about the situation at work, even when you're not actively dealing with it—like when you're at home or trying to relax?

Yeah, definitely. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I just can't seem to leave it at the plant. Even when I sit down in the evening and try to relax, I'm still completely wound up. 

I'll be lying in bed trying to get to sleep, and instead, I'm just replaying every single meeting in my head, thinking about how that new manager is picking apart my procedures. And because I'm dwelling on it so much at home, it messes me up the next day. I go in and start second-guessing those routine quality checks that I've done a million times without any issue. So, yes, it's just constantly on my mind.
When you’re feeling stressed about the situation at work, do you notice any physical symptoms, like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or trouble breathing?

No, not really. I mean, I feel tense and wound up, like I said, but I haven't noticed my heart racing or anything like that. I'm not sweating or having trouble breathing. It's just that constant feeling of being stressed out and on edge, but no real physical stuff like you're talking about.
Do you find that your worry about the situation at work feels constant or overwhelming, even when you're not actively thinking about it?

Well, I wouldn't say it's constant when I'm *not* thinking about it. It's more like... when I'm not distracted by something else, my mind just goes right back to the plant and that manager. If I'm busy doing something around the house or talking with my husband, I'm okay. But the second things get quiet, the worry is just right there waiting for me. So it's not overwhelming every single second of the day, but it's definitely always hovering in the background.
Do you feel like your worrying about the situation at work is something you can't control, even when you try to stop thinking about it?

No, I wouldn't say I completely lose control over it. I mean, it's hard to shake off, like I said, especially when it's quiet. But if I really force myself to go do something else—like if I get up and start cleaning, or turn on a show and really try to focus on it—I can usually get my mind off it for a bit. It's not like I'm completely powerless to stop it, it just takes a lot of effort to push it away.
Have you noticed any days where you feel down, hopeless, or lose interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work stress?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel hopeless or down in the dumps. I still enjoy the things I normally do, like spending time with my husband or just relaxing at home when I can get my mind off things. It's really just the stress and the worry about the plant that's bothering me, but it hasn't made me lose interest in my actual life or anything like that.
Have you been having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because you're worrying about the situation at work?

Yes, I definitely do. I end up lying awake just... replaying meetings in my head. Honestly, ever since this new operations manager started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I just can’t seem to leave work at work. I come home all wound up, I end up snapping at my husband, and then I'm stuck awake at night overthinking everything they said. And the worst part is how it carries over into the next day. I go in tired and stressed, and I start second-guessing routine quality calls that I used to make without any trouble at all.
Do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things other than work, even when there's nothing particularly stressful going on?

No, not really. It's pretty much just work. I mean, sure, I might worry about normal things here and there, like bills or my husband's health, but nothing out of the ordinary. When I'm away from work and not thinking about the plant, I feel fine. It's just that one situation that's got me so tied up in knots.
Do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worrying about multiple things in your life, even when there isn’t an obvious reason or specific stressor?

No, I think I just answered that, actually. It's really just the situation at the plant. I don't sit around worrying about everything else for no reason. If I'm stressed, there's a reason for it, and right now, that reason is work.
Do you ever feel anxious or worried about several different things at once, even when you're not at work or dealing with the situation with your manager?

I feel like we're going in circles here. Like I said, no. It's just the work stuff. I don't have this... general anxiety about everything in my life. When I'm not dealing with the plant or that new manager, I'm okay. It's just that one specific thing causing all this stress.
Do you often feel restless or like you're constantly on edge, even when there isn't an immediate problem at work?

No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely on edge when I'm dealing with the plant, but if I'm at home and not thinking about it... no, I wouldn't say I feel restless. It's really just tied to that one situation.
